Main.sentence: The Cuban thaw   ( ___E:Spanish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language)___ : deshielo cubano ,   .mw-parser-output .IPA-label-small{font-size:85%}.mw-parser-output .references .IPA-label-small,.mw-parser-output .infobox .IPA-label-small,.mw-parser-output .navbox .IPA-label-small{font-size:100%} pronounced [desˈʝelo kuˈβano] ) was a normalization of ___E:Cuba–United States relations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba%E2%80%93United_States_relations)___ from July 2015 to June 2017, ending a 54-year stretch of hostility between the nations.

In March 2016, ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ became the first ___E:U.S. president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ to visit ___E:Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba)___ since ___E:Calvin Coolidge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Coolidge)___ in 1928.  The ___E:diplomatic détente U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C3%A9tente)___ was reversed by the U.S. government – under both Presidents ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ and ___E:Joe Biden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden)___ – due to a variety of subsequent geopolitical issues.
Modern diplomatic relations are cold, stemming from historic conflict and divergent political ideologies.

The initial easing of relations was mediated by the ___E:Holy See U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See)___ ( ___E:Pope Francis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Francis)___ ) and hosted by ___E:Canada U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Canada)___ after multilateral dialogue with ___E:First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Secretary_of_the_Communist_Party_of_Cuba)___ ___E:Raúl Castro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ra%C3%BAl_Castro)___ in 2014.  A normalization agreement was put in place that year, easing the ___E:U.S. embargo against Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_embargo_against_Cuba)___ .

The agreement would lift restrictions on the ___E:Cuban travel ban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_embargo_against_Cuba#Travel_restrictions)___ , remittances to Cuba, and access to the ___E:Cuban financial system U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Cuba#Finance)___ .

The ___E:U.S. embassy in Havana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embassy_of_the_United_States,_Havana)___ and ___E:Cuban embassy in Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embassy_of_Cuba,_Washington,_D.C.)___ both re-opened, previously designated as latent " ___E:interests sections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Interests_Section_in_Havana)___ ".

In 2015, the U.S. waived Cuba's designation as a ___E:State Sponsors of Terrorism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Sponsors_of_Terrorism_(U.S._list))___ , in a major U.S. foreign policy divergence.
Relations deteriorated sharply over the status of ___E:human rights in Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights_in_Cuba)___ .

The election of President Trump in 2017 led to a reversal of accommodative U.S. foreign policy toward Cuba.   The U.S. embargo was significantly tightened with a travel ban preceding heightened restrictions on financial transactions benefiting the ___E:Cuban armed forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Revolutionary_Armed_Forces)___ .

The U.S. government further retaliated for protest crackdowns and human rights abuse ___E:in 2021 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Cuban_protests)___ and again ___E:in 2024 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_2024_Cuban_protests)___ .

Since the Cuban thaw, both nations have contested issues on counterterrorism, immigration, electoral interference, financial claims, ___E:fugitive extradition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_fugitives_in_Cuba)___ and ___E:Cuban foreign policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_Cuba)___ .

In May 2012, it was reported that the U.S. had declined a "spy swap" proposed by the Cuban government, wherein the remaining three of an original group of Cuban prisoners the U.S. had convicted of espionage known as the ___E:Cuban Five U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Five)___ , in prison in the U.S. since the 1990s, would be returned to Cuba in exchange for ___E:USAID U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USAID)___ contractor ___E:Alan Gross U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Gross)___ .

Gross had been imprisoned in Cuba for providing illegal cellphone chips of a type used by CIA agents, which are designed to evade detection,  in addition to computer equipment, satellite phones, and internet access to Cuba's Jewish community.
Despite initial U.S. refusals, the prisoner swap eventually took place in December 2014 following the President's announcement of intent to move towards normalized relations.

In addition to Gross, the swap included ___E:Rolando Sarraff Trujillo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolando_Sarraff_Trujillo)___ , a Cuban who had worked as an agent for American intelligence and had been in a Cuban prison for nearly 20 years.
Additionally, in early January 2015, the Cuban government began releasing a number of imprisoned dissidents, as requested by the United States.
On January 12, 2015, it was reported that all 53 dissidents had been released.

The prisoner swap marked the biggest shift in ___E:White House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House)___ policy towards Cuba since the imposition of the ___E:embargo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_embargo_against_Cuba)___ in 1962, and removed a key obstacle to bilateral relations.
Since the exchange, Gross has become a vocal advocate of the normalization of relations, even offering to visit Cuba again in support of such a result.
Although the Cuban trade embargo can only be ended by the U.S.
Congress, the Obama administration took executive action to ease some restrictions on travel to Cuba by U.S. citizens, as well as restrictions on the import and export of goods between each country.

In his ___E:2015 State of the Union Address U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_State_of_the_Union_Address)___ to ___E:Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress)___ , Obama called on lawmakers to lift the ___E:embargo against Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_embargo_against_Cuba)___ ,  a message he reiterated in ___E:2016 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_State_of_the_Union_Address)___ .

In February 2015, ___E:Conan O'Brien U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conan_O%27Brien)___ became the first American television personality to film in Cuba after the thaw, and only the third in more than half a century,  culminating in the first Conan Without Borders ___E:special U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_special)___ .

In May 2015, the ___E:Minnesota Orchestra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Orchestra)___ performed several concerts in Havana, the first professional U.S. orchestra to play in Cuba since 1999.

___E:Major League Baseball U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball)___ (MLB) held talks about playing ___E:spring training U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spring_training)___ games in Cuba in 2015, but lacked time to arrange them.  MLB Commissioner ___E:Rob Manfred U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Manfred)___ said on March 19, 2015, that the league would likely play an exhibition game in Cuba sometime in early 2016  and on March 22, 2016, the ___E:Tampa Bay Rays U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Bay_Rays)___ played an exhibition game against the ___E:Cuba national team U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba_national_baseball_team)___ at ___E:Estadio Latinoamericano U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_Latinoamericano)___ in Havana with U.S.
President Obama and Cuban leader Castro in attendance.

___E:Sun Country Airlines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Country_Airlines)___ began operating charter flights between New York's ___E:John F. Kennedy International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_International_Airport)___ and Havana's ___E:José Martí International Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mart%C3%AD_International_Airport)___ in March 2015.  On May 5, 2015, the United States granted approval to four companies to offer chartered ___E:ferry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferry)___ service between Miami and Cuba.  In March 2016, ___E:Carnival Cruise Line U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnival_Cruise_Line)___ received permission from Cuba to resume cruises from Miami to Havana for the first time in fifty years.

Cuba, however, still prohibited the Cuban-born from returning by sea, and Carnival therefore refused to accept reservations from the Cuban-born. Following public protests against such an exclusionary policy, Carnival told the Cuban authorities it would not sail unless the policy was changed, the Cuban government relented, and the first Carnival cruise sailed from Miami on May 1, 2016.

Between January and May 2015, the number of Americans visiting Cuba who had no family ties there was 36% higher than during the same months in 2014.  A report by the ___E:Pew Research Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pew_Research_Center)___ found that the number of Cubans entering the U.S. in 2015 was 78% higher than in 2014.
It has been said that the United States–Cuban thaw was spurred by Cuba's main international partner, Venezuela, experiencing sharp economic decline.
Venezuela subsidized the government of Cuba, following the oil price drop resulting from the ___E:2010s oil glut U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010s_oil_glut)___ , could no longer afford to do so.
On January 21, 2015, the United States and Cuba began bilateral talks in Havana to discuss further normalization issues.

The U.S. delegation led by ___E:U.S. Assistant Secretary of State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Assistant_Secretary_of_State)___ ___E:Roberta S. Jacobson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberta_S._Jacobson)___ , and ___E:Josefina Vidal Ferreiro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josefina_Vidal_Ferreiro)___ , Cuba's head of North American affairs, sat down for the first day of closed-door talks in the capital's Convention Center.
The talks reportedly centered around migration policy.

In particular, Cuban representatives urged the U.S. to end its immigration privileges to Cuban refugees, also known as the ___E:wet feet, dry feet policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wet_feet,_dry_feet_policy)___ , [needs update] which allows any fleeing Cuban citizens U.S. residency and ___E:citizenship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_citizen)___ , as long as they are found on U.S. soil and not at sea.  Reuters reported that civilian uncertainty about the status of ___E:U.S. immigration policy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigration_to_the_United_States)___ following the thaw was promoting a surge of emigrants fleeing Cuba for the U.S.

In regard to U.S. interests, the U.S. delegation made it clear that "improved human rights conditions, including freedom of expression and assembly", remain a central element of U.S. policy in normalizing U.S.–Cuban relations.
Furthermore, despite Cuban objections, the U.S. stated that it will stand by its Cuban migration policy under the ___E:Cuban Adjustment Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Adjustment_Act)___ .

A second round of talks took place in ___E:Washington, D.C. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C.)___ , late in February 2015. Negotiators described the talks as productive and said several issues were close to resolution.

However, the issue of Cuba's listing among state sponsors of terrorism by the U.S. government remained a significant sticking point, although Cuban diplomat ___E:Josefina Vidal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josefina_Vidal)___ said its removal was not strictly a precondition to reopening embassies.
A third round of talks were held in Havana from March 16–17, 2015. However, the talks ended abruptly after just a day, without any public comment.

Obama and Castro themselves met at the ___E:Summit of the Americas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summit_of_the_Americas)___ in ___E:Panama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama)___ on April 10–11, where Castro delivered an address praising Obama and apologizing for blaming his government for the ongoing U.S. embargo.

After meeting with Obama, Castro called for the reopening of the embassies, while both leaders said they were looking forward to more direct engagement between Cuba and the United States despite their differences.

The Vatican and ___E:Pope Francis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Francis)___ played a symbolic but substantial role in helping facilitate the normalization of diplomatic relation between the U.S. and Cuba. The Catholic Church has remained in close cooperation with Havana even after the ___E:1959 revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Revolution)___ .
In addition to Cuba's concern over U.S. migration policy, the Cuban delegation assured the U.S. that normalization talks would not yield significant changes unless Cuba is removed from the U.S.
State Department's list of ___E:state sponsors of terrorism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Sponsors_of_Terrorism)___ .

Cuba was one of four countries on the list, the other three being ___E:Iran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran)___ , ___E:Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan)___ , and ___E:Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria)___ .
The U.S. government said that it had begun an intelligence review in order to evaluate whether Cuba can be removed from the list.

On April 14, 2015, President Obama informed the ___E:U.S. Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress)___ that he had decided to lift the designation of Cuba as a state sponsor of terrorism because "the government of Cuba has not provided any support for international terrorism during the preceding six-month period", and it "has provided assurances that it will not support acts of international terrorism in the future".
The U.S.
Congress could have blocked this by passing legislation within 45 days, but no member of Congress even introduced such legislation, and Cuba was officially removed from the list on May 29, 2015.
On May 20, 2015, the Cuban government opened a bank account in the United States, enabling it to do non-cash business in the United States for the first time since the embargo began.

Cuba and the United States officially resumed full diplomatic relations at midnight on July 20, 2015, with the " ___E:Cuban interests section U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embassy_of_Cuba_in_Washington,_D.C.)___ " in ___E:Washington, D.C. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C.)___ , and the " ___E:U.S. interests section U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Interests_Section_in_Havana)___ " in ___E:Havana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Havana)___ being upgraded to embassies.
A ceremony was held at the Cuban Embassy to raise the ___E:flag of Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_of_Cuba)___ , with U.S.

Secretary of State ___E:John Kerry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry)___ and Cuban Foreign Minister ___E:Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Rodr%C3%ADguez_Parrilla)___ holding a joint news conference afterward at which they emphasized both the step forward in bilateral relations and the remaining political differences between the Cuban and U.S. governments.
Kerry flew to Cuba in late July for a ceremony at which the ___E:flag of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_of_the_United_States)___ was raised over the US Embassy in Havana.
Cuban dissidents, however, were not invited to attend the flag raising ceremony.

In September 2015, Cuban diplomat ___E:José Ramón Cabañas Rodríguez U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Ram%C3%B3n_Caba%C3%B1as_Rodr%C3%ADguez)___ was appointed the first ___E:Ambassador of Cuba to the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ambassadors_of_Cuba_to_the_United_States)___ in 50 years.

On January 28, 2015, while attending a meeting of Latin American leaders in ___E:San José, Costa Rica U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jos%C3%A9,_Costa_Rica)___ , Cuban leader Raúl Castro asserted that the United States should return the ___E:Guantanamo Bay Naval Base U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guantanamo_Bay_Naval_Base)___ and lift the embargo on Cuba if relations were to be considered fully normalized.

The White House responded the next day, saying that it had no intention to return the base. White House spokesman ___E:Josh Earnest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Earnest)___ indicated any such move is out of the question. "The President does believe that the ___E:prison at Guantánamo Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guantanamo_Bay_detention_camp)___ should be closed down, but the ___E:naval base U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guantanamo_Bay_Naval_Base)___ is not something that we wish to be closed."  This issue has yet to be resolved.

The United States government stated specific goals in improving trade with Cuba. ___E:Roberta Jacobson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberta_S._Jacobson)___ , an American diplomat, suggested bolstering ___E:Internet access U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_in_Cuba)___ and mobile phone service in Cuba to help its integration into the ___E:world economy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_economy)___ .

This provided American telecommunication companies including ___E:Verizon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verizon_Wireless)___ and ___E:Sprint U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sprint_Corporation)___ with a new market in Cuba.  By July 20, 2016, US companies ___E:Airbnb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbnb)___ and ___E:Netflix U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix)___ were operating in Cuba as well.

The United States sought to increase revenue from ___E:tourism in Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_Cuba)___ by lifting traveling restrictions which can be used for purchase of American agricultural and manufacturing exports to Cuba.  On March 20, 2016, ___E:Starwood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starwood_Hotels_and_Resorts)___ became the first US company to sign a deal with Cuba since the 1959 revolution and agreed to manage two Havana hotels which had formerly been owned by the Cuban government.

The first of these hotels opened three months later on June 27.  A number of American companies support further economic ties with Cuba, as do advocacy groups like ___E:Engage Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engage_Cuba)___ .

On December 11, 2015, the United States and Cuba agreed to restore postal service between the two countries for the first time since 1963.  A week later, on December 17, 2015 – the first anniversary of D17 – an agreement was reached to re-establish regularly scheduled flights between the U.S. and Cuba for the first time since the ___E:Cuban Missile Crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Missile_Crisis)___ .
The agreement, which allows for 110 flights a day, took effect on February 16, 2016.  Mail service between the two countries resumed on March 17, 2016.

On July 7, 2016, it was announced that eight US airline companies had been given tentative approval to fly to airports in Cuba and that flights, which would be limited to educational trips, would begin as early as September.

On August 31, 2016, ___E:JetBlue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JetBlue)___ became the first US commercial airline in more than 50 years to land a plane carrying US passengers at a Cuban airport when ___E:Flight 387 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JetBlue_Flight_387)___ took off from ___E:Fort Lauderdale, Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Lauderdale,_Florida)___ and landed in ___E:Santa Clara, Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Clara,_Cuba)___ .

More flights have since followed,     and two planes from JetBlue and American Airlines also made history by landing in the capital city of Havana on November 28, 2016,   marking the first time in more than 50 years that a US commercial flight landed in Havana.
By November 2017, however, several airline companies had quit doing flights to Cuba.

President Obama arrived in Cuba for a three-day visit on March 20, 2016.  Obama headed a delegation of between 800 and 1,200, including businesspeople and congressional leaders who had helped in establishing the 2014 normalization deal.

Obama was the ___E:first sitting U.S. president to visit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_international_trips_made_by_the_President_of_the_United_States)___ Cuba since ___E:Calvin Coolidge in 1928 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign_policy_of_the_Calvin_Coolidge_administration)___ .

Obama said that he would only visit Cuba if he could meet with ___E:Cuban dissidents U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_dissident_movement)___ : "If I go on a visit, then part of the deal is that I get to talk to everybody.

I've made it very clear in my conversations directly with Cuban leader Raúl Castro that we would continue to reach out to those who want to broaden the scope for, you know, free expression inside of Cuba."

On April 22, 2016, it was announced that travel restrictions on U.S. ___E:commercial vessels U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercial_vessel)___ had been lifted and that the ___E:Carnival Cruise Line U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnival_Cruise_Line)___ could travel to Cuba.

On May 1, 2016, the ___E:MV Adonia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MV_Adonia)___ , a ___E:cruise ship U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cruise_ship)___ operated by Carnival subsidiary ___E:Fathom Travel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fathom_(cruise_line))___ , departed from Miami and docked in ___E:Havana Bay U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Havana_Bay)___ , marking the first time in nearly 40 years that a U.S. passenger ship sailed from the U.S. to Cuba.  Carnival said that the Adonia would go from Miami to Havana every other week.

Two other Miami-based cruise lines, ___E:Royal Caribbean U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Caribbean_International)___ and ___E:Norwegian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norwegian_Cruise_Line)___ , were interested in running cruises to Cuba and sought Cuban government authorization.

A number of Florida ___E:ferry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferry)___ companies received authorization from the ___E:U.S. Department of the Treasury U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Department_of_the_Treasury)___ to begin service to Cuba, but the companies were waiting on Cuban government permission.
In June 2019, the ___E:Trump administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_presidency_of_Donald_Trump)___ made a policy reversal by banning cruise ship travel to Cuba.

___E:Raúl Castro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ra%C3%BAl_Castro)___ , the ___E:First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Secretary_of_the_Communist_Party_of_Cuba)___ , served as the leader since 2011 and one of the leaders of the ___E:Cuban Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Revolution)___ of the 1950s, declared in 2013 that "a slow and orderly transfer of the leadership of the revolution to the new generations" was already in progress.

Castro pledged not to seek reelection in 2018.  In announcing the agreement in December 2014, Castro struck a balance between praising the ___E:Marxist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marxism)___ revolution that brought him and his brother ___E:Fidel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidel_Castro)___ to power almost 60 years prior and extolling the benefits that would be brought about by improved relations with the United States, namely the end of the ___E:Cuban embargo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_embargo)___ .

Fidel Castro appeared to welcome the thaw between Cuba and the United States in a statement published by Granma on January 26, 2015. Despite saying that he "does not trust United States policies", he stated, "We will always defend cooperation and friendship with all the peoples of the world, among them our political adversaries."
However, later in 2016, Fidel Castro asserted his criticism of Obama, acknowledging his own anger with Obama's March trip to Cuba in which he called for Cubans to look toward the future.
A week after the trip, Castro wrote a sternly worded letter admonishing Obama to read up on Cuban history, and declaring that "we don't need the empire to give us anything."
In December 2014, Raúl Castro publicly thanked Pope Francis and the Catholic Church for their role in the secret talks that led to the U.S.–Cuban prisoner exchange.
According to Church officials within Cuba, several plans to build Catholic churches, which have been blocked since the revolution in 1959, are being processed.
The first church is to be built in ___E:Sandino U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandino,_Cuba)___ .
It will be the first Catholic church to be built in Cuba since 1959.

At a ___E:CELAC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CELAC)___ meeting in 2015, Raúl Castro gave a speech claiming "Cuba will continue to defend the ideas for which our people have assumed the greatest sacrifices and risks." In that speech, he detailed the history of Cuba's foreign relations.

Throughout the speech, he condemned the United States' history of ___E:manifest destiny U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manifest_destiny)___ , detailing a basic history of American and Cuban relations.

After talking about the United States' policy in Cuba, he went on to condemn the United States' assistance in installing the "terrible dictatorships in 20 countries, 12 of them simultaneously", referring to the United States' supporting of Latin American dictatorships.
Following that, Castro detailed Cuba's history following the ___E:Cuban Revolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Revolution)___ .

But despite his prior backlash against the United States, Castro summarized his speech by praising the recent improvements in American-Cuban relations, and wondered why "the countries of the two Americas, the North and the South, fight together against terrorism, drug trafficking and organized crime, without politically biased positions."
The Cuban thaw has received a mixed reception among politicians in the United States.
Prominent critics include Senator ___E:Marco Rubio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Rubio)___ of ___E:Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida)___ .

Rubio, a ___E:Cuban-American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_American)___ ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ , said that "diplomatic recognition [would] provide legitimacy to a government that doesn't deserve it."   The ___E:2014 congressional elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_elections,_2014)___ were a month prior to the announcement of the thaw.

Senator ___E:Bob Menendez U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Menendez)___ , a Cuban-American ___E:Democrat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ from ___E:New Jersey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey)___ and chairman of the ___E:Senate Foreign Relations Committee U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Foreign_Relations)___ was an early critic of Obama's decision to normalize relations with Cuba. Writing in USA Today on December 17, Menendez criticized Obama "for compromising on bedrock U.S. values", charging that the Obama administration "has wrongly rewarded a totalitarian regime and thrown the Cuban regime an economic lifeline".

Among the few other Democrats who have criticized Obama over the shift in relations with Cuba are two members of the House of Representatives: ___E:Albio Sires U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albio_Sires)___  and ___E:Debbie Wasserman-Schultz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debbie_Wasserman-Schultz)___ .

Congressional opponents of the new Cuba policy vowed to try to block its implementation, with Rubio announcing he would hold up the confirmation of any ___E:U.S. ambassador to Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Ambassador_to_Cuba)___ whom Obama might nominate.

Republican Senator ___E:Ted Cruz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Cruz)___ of ___E:Texas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas)___ described the policy as a "tragic mistake."  However, the ___E:Associated Press U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press)___ reported that business groups like the ___E:U.S. Chamber of Commerce U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Chamber_of_Commerce)___ would likely apply pressure on congressmen to accept the diplomatic thaw, and ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ Senator ___E:Jeff Flake U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Flake)___ of ___E:Arizona U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona)___ , a supporter of the shift, predicted many congressmen would come around.

Like Senator Flake, Senator ___E:Rand Paul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rand_Paul)___ , a Republican from Kentucky, supports the thaw on the grounds that increased trade relations will benefit both Cubans and Americans.
Senator Paul, in response to Senator Rubio, argued that "Senator Rubio is acting like an isolationist", and that, "The 50-year embargo just hasn't worked.
If the goal is regime change, it sure doesn't seem to be working."
Similarly, Obama's former Secretary of State and 2016 presidential candidate ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ strongly endorsed the decision.
Clinton has argued that the embargo "had propped up the Castro government because they could blame all of the country's problems on the United States.
Moreover, the embargo did not have any impact on freedom of speech, freedom of expression, or on freeing political prisoners."

A survey conducted by ___E:Pew Research Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pew_Research_Center)___ in January 2016 found that 63% of Americans approved of Obama's decision to re-establish diplomatic relations with Cuba, while 28% disapproved.
The study found that Democrats (74%) and Independents (67%) were more likely to support the re-established relations; 40% of Republicans approved.
The study also found that 66% of Americans supported ending the trade embargo against Cuba, while 28% disapproved.

Support for both the re-establishment of relations and the lifting of the trade embargo was seen broadly amongst all racial and ethnic groups (62% of whites, 64% of blacks, and 65% of Hispanics) and amongst all age-brackets, however younger Americans were more likely to support it than older Americans.

Americans who were college or university graduates (77%) overwhelmingly supported the restoration of relations, while people with only some college education (59%) or only high school education (53%) were less likely to support it. Despite broad support for the re-establishment of diplomatic relations and the end of the trade embargo, only 32% of Americans surveyed believed that Cuba would become "more democratic" over the next several years, with 60% believing the situation in Cuba will remain the same.

International reactions were overwhelmingly positive, with ___E:Radio Poland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Poland)___ having reported that the ___E:Polish foreign ministry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs_(Poland))___ is encouraging Washington to go further and lift the embargo.
___E:China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China)___ , also one of Cuba's closest allies, welcomed the resumption of diplomatic relations between Cuba and the United States.

___E:Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel)___ was one of the few countries not to issue a statement welcoming the change, and it was reported that the Israeli Foreign Ministry is "miffed" at having been caught off guard by the change.  ___E:Cuba–Israel relations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba%E2%80%93Israel_relations)___ have been icy since the 1960s, and Israel has been the only country to consistently side with the US against ___E:UN resolutions criticizing the embargo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_embargo_against_Cuba#Criticism_of_embargo_laws_and_rules)___ .

Several ___E:Latin American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_America)___ leaders publicly welcomed the thaw, with ___E:Venezuelan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela)___ President ___E:Nicolás Maduro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicol%C3%A1s_Maduro)___ hailing Obama's move toward normalization as a "valiant and historically necessary gesture", despite being a regular critic of U.S. policy.

Colombian Liberal ex-President ___E:Ernesto Samper U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernesto_Samper)___ in his capacity as President of ___E:UNASUR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNASUR)___ said that "this was very good news, not only for Cuba but for the entire region". ___E:Juan Carlos Varela U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Carlos_Varela)___ , the conservative President of Panama, said that in the ___E:7th Summit of the Americas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/7th_Summit_of_the_Americas)___ to be held in his country after April 7, 2015, it will be possible to "achieve the dream of a united region".

The ___E:Canadian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada)___ government, which maintained ___E:more positive relations with Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada%E2%80%93Cuba_relations)___ than the United States did during and after the Cold War, also responded favorably, with Foreign Minister ___E:John Baird U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Baird_(Canadian_politician))___ suggesting to The Atlantic commentator ___E:Jeffrey Goldberg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Goldberg)___ that the policy shift could help "transform" Cuba for the better.

Media sources, which were quick to dub the sudden turnaround in relations the "Cuban thaw",  have predicted that it will lead to a wide variety of social and economic benefits for the two countries, as well as some less obvious impacts.

Newsweek reported that the stock market jumped once elements of the Cuban thaw were reported.  ___E:Reuters U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuters)___ reported that the thaw would "make it more likely the Cuban government will extradite ___E:fugitives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fugitive)___ sought by U.S. officials."  The ___E:Associated Press U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Associated_Press)___ reported environmentalist concerns that the thaw would lead to the opening of "one of the most prolific oil and gas basins on the planet", which sits off the coast of Cuba.  Bloomberg News reported that the thaw would even benefit ___E:Major League Baseball U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Baseball)___ , with teams gaining major new opportunities to sign Cuban players.
There were reports on how the Cuban thaw affected Cuban society, including its real estate market and greater emphasis on English language education.

The New Republic deemed the Cuban thaw to be "Obama's finest foreign policy achievement."  The Indonesian journal Strategic Review proposed that Obama could follow the model of normalization of relations which his predecessor ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ had done with ___E:United States-Vietnam relations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States-Vietnam_relations)___ .

Granma , Cuba's state newspaper, published numerous articles regarding the Cuban thaw. It stated that "International public opinion supports removal of Cuba from U.S. list of state sponsors of terrorism," and that "[t]he decision is recognized as an important step in advancing President Obama's policy change to improve relations between the two countries."  Additionally, they stated that "[t]he Cuban government recognizes the just decision taken by the President of the United States to eliminate Cuba from a list on which it never should have been included" and reiterated that Cuba "rejects and condemns all acts of terrorism in all their forms and manifestations, as well as any action that is intended to instigate, support, finance or conceal terrorist acts."
In broader culture, the Cuban thaw served as inspiration the artwork The Pact by leading Cuban-American Contemporary artist ___E:Josignacio U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josignacio)___ .

Considered a significant work in his oeuvre, The Pact depicts the widely circulated media image of President Obama with Raúl Castro in Panama while adding the symbolic silhouettes of the ___E:American Bald Eagle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Bald_Eagle)___ , ___E:Fidel Castro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidel_Castro)___ , as well as the image of Cuban national hero ___E:José Martí U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Mart%C3%AD)___ .

The work was acquired by the ___E:Tampa Museum of Art U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa_Museum_of_Art)___ due to its cultural significance in capturing the historic resumption of diplomatic relations between both nations, as well as the ___E:historic links in Tampa to Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ybor_City)___ .
The museum's acquisition of The Pact was covered by Diario Las Américas , the second oldest media outlet in the United States dedicated to Spanish-language readers.

The ___E:diplomatic détente U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C3%A9tente)___ was reversed by the U.S. government – under both Presidents ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ and ___E:Joe Biden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden)___ – due to a variety of subsequent geopolitical issues.
Modern diplomatic relations are cold, stemming from historic conflict and divergent political ideologies.

On June 16, 2017, President Trump issued a ___E:presidential memorandum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_memorandum)___ reversing some aspects of the Obama administration's actions regarding U.S. relations with Cuba, and characterizing them as "terrible and misguided".
He announced a prohibition on American money going to the Cuban military.

In addition, he removed permission for individual "people-to-people" travel to Cuba by Americans, while leaving in place travel permission for organized "educational" groups, family visits and other categories.

On November 8, 2017, the White House announced that the new regulations would take effect starting November 9, 2017.  The Cuban ___E:Minister of Foreign Affairs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minister_of_Foreign_Affairs_(Cuba))___ , ___E:Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Rodr%C3%ADguez_Parrilla)___ , stated that the Cuban state "rejected" the sanctions, which it viewed as aiming to suffocate the island's economy and harm its living standards in order to achieve political concessions.
In September 2019, further changes were made in relation to remittances.

The ___E:Biden administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Joe_Biden)___ had initially continued the sanctions from the Trump administration against ___E:Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba)___ .
In May 2022, some of the sanctions were reversed, with policy changes such as expansion of flights to Cuba and resumption of a family reunification program.

In 2024, the ___E:Treasury Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_the_Treasury)___ published details of President Biden's plan to support Cuba's private sector and internet freedom.

On 14 January 2025, the Biden administration temporarily removed Cuba from the ___E:State Sponsors of Terrorism list U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Sponsors_of_Terrorism_(U.S._list))___ , as part of a prisoner release deal.   In addition to re-designating the island as a state sponsor of terrorism for a third time in 2025, the State Department announced further sanctions against Cuban military contractors and further restricted Cuba's access to the U.S. dollar.

U.S. ___E:Homeland Security U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Homeland_Security)___ and ___E:Coast Guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Coast_Guard)___ soon thereafter restricted immigration of ___E:economic refugees from Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_exodus)___ , along with Haiti, Nicaragua, and Venezuela.

The U.S. re-activiated Title III of the ___E:Helms–Burton Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helms%E2%80%93Burton_Act)___ , an international deterrent against foreign investment in Cuba.   The U.S. government halted foreign aid funding, expanded visa restrictions, and formally cautioned against Cuban forced labor in February.

President Trump issued a ___E:presidential directive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_memorandum)___ in July for greater enforcement of the ___E:Cuban travel ban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_embargo_against_Cuba#Travel_restrictions)___ , further isolating the ___E:tourism industry of Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism_in_Cuba)___ .
The U.S. government banned Cuban leader Díaz-Canel along with two ministers from entering the U.S., later restricting access the Cuban luxury real estate sector.
